150.status: Original RDA WG output and recommendations consulted in sections I-ADOPT Framework (Figs 2–5), Six Key Recommendations for Variable Representations, and Supporting Outputs. Compare older guidance with 1.1.0 formal terms. The guidance recommends component terminology identifiers and excludes additional units, instruments, methods and geographic metadata from the framework. Those can be associated using other models. Six recommendations are guidance for descriptive practice. No blanket audit of linked external terminologies, applications or tools.

IADOPT-VARIABLE-ENTITY-ROLES.definition: For an individual variable, identify the property and the entity it characterizes. Preserve an entity that contains the measured entity as its matrix, and any other entity that provides context. The same entity may fill different roles in different variables.
IADOPT-VARIABLE-ENTITY-ROLES.why_new: Row 25 distinguishes a property and its subject. A named water measurement supplies a particular medium. Neither preserves the distinct matrix and other contextual entity roles for the same individual variable. Row 647 applies roles to a set and row 648 identifies a constraint's target.
IADOPT-VARIABLE-ENTITY-ROLES.locator: I-ADOPT 1.1.0 Turtle lines 180–186, 196–203, 213–219, 229–235, 279–289 and 311–324: hasContextObject, hasMatrix ⊑ hasContextObject, hasObjectOfInterest, hasProperty, Entity, Property and Variable. RDA 2022 recommendations, Figure 3 (illustration).
IADOPT-VARIABLE-ENTITY-ROLES.example: In the RDA oyster example the chemical is measured, flesh contains it, the oyster supplies additional context, and wet qualifies the flesh. A receiving client can preserve which entity played each role.
IADOPT-VARIABLE-ENTITY-ROLES.negative_test: A medium alone, equipment that hosts a detector, an item's location during acquisition, or a list of concepts applicable to a set does not establish all three role types on one variable.

IADOPT-COMPOSITE-ENTITY-ROLES.label: Interchangeable and role-specific participants in a composite observable entity
IADOPT-COMPOSITE-ENTITY-ROLES.definition: Describe a composite entity in a variable through the roles of its constituent entities. Preserve interchangeable parts when order has no meaning. For an asymmetric relationship, distinguish numerator from denominator in a fraction, or source from sink in a flow.
IADOPT-COMPOSITE-ENTITY-ROLES.why_new: Equipment containment and individual power or signal ratios do not record whether interchanging the participants preserves the observable's meaning across domains. A variable set groups descriptions rather than entities within one description.
IADOPT-COMPOSITE-ENTITY-ROLES.locator: I-ADOPT 1.1.0 Turtle lines 188–194, 205–211, 221–227, 237–243, 253–259, 266–270 and 297–309: hasDenominator, hasNumerator, hasPart, hasSource, hasTarget, AsymmetricSystem, SymmetricSystem and System.
IADOPT-COMPOSITE-ENTITY-ROLES.example: Illustrative application: exchanging the names of two sites preserves the meaning of the distance between them. Reversing the source and sink changes the definition of flow from one site to the other.
IADOPT-COMPOSITE-ENTITY-ROLES.negative_test: An unspecified percentage, unit denominator, signed number, installed assembly, digital record group or equipment source/sink tag alone does not identify the constituent entities and their roles in an observable.

discriminating_examples: RDA Figure 3 names concentration of a particular chemical in wet oyster flesh. Chemical, flesh and oyster occupy different roles. Wet qualifies the flesh. This checks the distinction between the two new candidates and the old constraint row.

RDA Figure 4 decomposes the date of a specified recent laboratory test. Figure 5 uses a qualitative property for a cell shape. These examples establish that an identified characteristic can be a quality or relate to a process. They do not define field encoding, instrument identity or a record validating an actual test.

In the pinned release, hasDenominator/hasNumerator assign Entity participants in a fraction, and hasSource/hasTarget assign Entity participants in a flux. A numerical unit ratio, per-cell voltage, rated capacity denominator or signal reference left unspecified does not by itself identify such participants.

Existing row 597 accounts for statistical function, and 647 and 648 preserve set-level applicability and what a constraint targets. Guidance to annotate components is preserved on rows 24 and 493. These checks yielded two other native distinctions rather than duplicating these rows.
